script:
Clerk: Hello, how can I help you?
Customer: Hi. I bought this jacket last week, but it's too small. Can I exchange it for a bigger size?
Clerk: Of course. Do you have the receipt?
Customer: Yes, here it is.
Clerk: Thank you. Unfortunately, we don't have a large in this color. We have it in blue or black, though.
Customer: Oh, that's a pity. I'll take the black one, then.
Clerk: Great. Since the black one is ten dollars cheaper, I'll give you the difference back.

qs.q: What does the customer want to do?
opts: Exchange a jacket for a larger size
Get a refund for a lost receipt
qs.why: The jacket is too small, so the customer asks to exchange it for a bigger size.

qs.q: Why can't the customer get the same jacket in a bigger size?
opts: There is no large in that color
The jacket is out of fashion
qs.why: The clerk says there is no large in this color.

qs.q: What will the clerk give back to the customer?
qs.why: The black jacket is ten dollars cheaper, so the clerk returns the difference.

script:
Guest: Excuse me, I'm calling from room 305. The air conditioning isn't working, and it's very hot.
Reception: I'm sorry to hear that, sir. I'll send someone up right away.
Guest: Thank you. Also, the people next door are playing loud music.
Reception: I apologise. I'll call them and ask them to turn it down. If you'd prefer, we can move you to a quieter room on the fifth floor.
Guest: Actually, I'd like that. Could you sort it out as soon as possible?
Reception: Certainly. A porter will bring your new key in ten minutes.

qs.q: Why is the guest calling reception?
opts: To report problems in his room
To ask about his lost key
qs.why: He reports a broken air conditioner and loud music.

qs.q: Where could the guest move to?
opts: A room on the fifth floor
qs.why: Reception offers a quieter room on the fifth floor, and he accepts.

qs.q: What does 'turn it down' mean in this conversation?
qs.why: Asking the neighbors to turn the music down means making it quieter.

script: Hi, Maria, this is David from Delta Supplies. I'm calling about your order of two hundred office chairs. Unfortunately, there's been a delay at the factory, so the chairs won't arrive on Friday as planned. They should be here by next Wednesday instead. I'm really sorry about that. If you need them sooner, we can send fifty chairs by express delivery at no extra cost. Please call me back before three o'clock today so I can arrange it. My number is five five five, oh one four two. Thanks, and talk soon.

qs.q: Why is David calling?
opts: To tell Maria about a delay in her order
qs.why: There is a delay at the factory.

qs.q: When will the chairs probably arrive?
qs.why: They should be there by next Wednesday.

qs.q: What does David offer to do?
opts: Give a discount on the whole order
Send part of the order by express delivery at no extra cost
Send fifty extra chairs for free
qs.why: He can send fifty chairs by express delivery at no extra cost.

script: My best friend Laura is moving to Canada next month, and I'm feeling quite sad about it. We've known each other since primary school, and we've never lived in different cities. Of course, I'm happy for her because she got a great job. But I'll miss our Saturday coffees. We've promised to keep in touch by video call every Sunday. Although the time difference might be a problem, I think we'll work it out. And I'm planning to visit her next summer, so I have something to look forward to.

qs.q: How does the speaker feel about Laura's move?
qs.why: She is sad, but also happy for Laura.

qs.q: Why is Laura moving to Canada?
qs.why: She got a great job.

qs.q: What does 'work it out' mean here?
qs.why: They will find a way to deal with the time difference.

script:
Agent: So, this is the living room. As you can see, it gets plenty of natural light.
Tenant: It's lovely. How much is the rent again?
Agent: It's fourteen hundred a month, and utilities are not included. You'd also need to pay a deposit equal to one month's rent.
Tenant: That's a bit more than I expected. Is there any room for negotiation?
Agent: I can't lower the rent, but the landlord might be willing to include parking, provided you sign a two-year lease.
Tenant: Hmm. I'll think it over and call you tomorrow.

qs.q: What are the speakers mainly discussing?
opts: The conditions for renting an apartment
How to decorate a living room
qs.why: The agent shows the apartment and talks about rent, deposit and lease.

qs.q: What is needed to get parking included?
qs.why: Parking may be included provided the tenant signs a two-year lease.

qs.q: What does 'think it over' mean?
qs.why: The tenant will consider the offer and call tomorrow.

script: In technology news today, a European company has unveiled a battery that, it says, can charge a smartphone in just five minutes. The company says the battery will be available in phones from next spring. Experts, however, are cautious. They point out that very fast charging can wear out batteries more quickly, which means users might have to replace their phones sooner. The firm insists that its new design solves this problem and has promised to publish independent test results by the end of the year.

qs.q: What is the news mainly about?
opts: A new app for saving energy
qs.why: A new battery charges a phone in five minutes.

qs.q: What has the company promised to do by the end of the year?
qs.why: It promised to publish independent test results.

qs.q: Why are experts cautious?
opts: Fast charging may shorten battery life
qs.why: They say fast charging can wear out batteries more quickly.

script: May I have your attention, please. The eight-fifteen train to Boston has been cancelled because of a signal failure near Providence. Passengers holding tickets for this service can board the nine o'clock train instead, which will stop at all stations. If you'd rather not travel today, you can get a full refund at the ticket office or online. Please note that seat reservations on the nine o'clock train are not required, but it may be crowded. We apologise for the inconvenience and appreciate your understanding.

qs.q: What is the announcement about?
opts: A cancelled train and the options available
qs.why: The train is cancelled, and the announcement explains alternatives.

qs.q: What caused the cancellation?
qs.why: It was cancelled because of a signal failure near Providence.

qs.q: Why might the nine o'clock train be crowded?
opts: It will also carry passengers from the cancelled train
qs.why: The announcement says it may be crowded; the likely reason is that ticket holders from the cancelled train can also board it.

script:
Interviewer: Thanks for coming in, Priya. Could you tell me about your previous job?
Priya: Of course. For three years I worked as a customer service agent at a telecom company. I dealt with around fifty calls a day.
Interviewer: And what was the biggest challenge?
Priya: Probably angry customers. At first I found it stressful, but I learnt to stay calm and listen carefully. In the end, I received the employee of the year award.
Interviewer: Impressive. Why do you want to leave?
Priya: I'm looking for more responsibility, and I'd love to lead a team one day.

qs.q: What kind of conversation is this?
qs.why: The interviewer asks about her previous job and why she wants to leave.

qs.q: What was the biggest challenge in Priya's previous job?
qs.why: She says the biggest challenge was angry customers.

qs.q: Why does Priya want to leave her job?
qs.why: She is looking for more responsibility and wants to lead a team.

script:
Manager: Okay, let's go through what happened. Ravi, can you walk us through the timeline?
Ravi: Sure. At two in the morning, the payment service started timing out. Monitoring picked it up, but the alert went to a mailbox nobody checks overnight, so we only found out at six.
Manager: So the outage lasted four hours?
Ravi: Roughly, yes. The root cause was an expired certificate. We've renewed it, and we're setting up automatic renewals so this doesn't crop up again.
Manager: Good. Let's also fix the alert routing. Otherwise, we'll be in the same boat next time.

qs.q: What is the meeting mainly about?
qs.why: They review the timeline and cause of an outage.

qs.q: Why did the team find out about the problem late?
opts: The alert went to a mailbox no one checks at night
qs.why: The alert was sent to a mailbox nobody checks overnight.

qs.q: What does 'we'll be in the same boat' mean?
opts: We'll be on a trip together
We'll face the same difficult situation
qs.why: It means they will be in the same bad situation if the routing isn't fixed.

script: If you're still using the same password for several accounts, you're taking a serious risk. Here's the thing: when one website gets hacked, criminals try those stolen details everywhere else. That's why I'd strongly recommend a password manager. It generates long, random passwords and fills them in for you, so you only need to remember one master password. Admittedly, it takes a little while to set up, but once you've got the hang of it, you'll wonder how you managed without. Also, switch on two-factor authentication wherever possible, because even the best password can be stolen.

qs.q: What is the speaker's main message?
opts: How to protect your online accounts
How to memorise passwords without any tools
qs.why: He recommends a password manager and two-factor authentication.

qs.q: Why is reusing a password risky?
opts: Criminals try stolen details on other sites
qs.why: When one site is hacked, criminals try the same details elsewhere.

qs.q: What does 'get the hang of it' mean?
opts: learn how to do it well
qs.why: It means becoming comfortable and skilled at using something.

script: A major retailer in the United States has announced that it will trial a four-day working week for its office staff, without cutting salaries. The company says the pilot, which will run for six months, is aimed at improving morale and cutting staff turnover. Critics argue that employees may simply cram the same workload into fewer days, leading to burnout. Nevertheless, some similar experiments abroad have reported that productivity stays the same or even rises. The results will be reviewed in March before any permanent decision is made.

qs.q: What has the retailer announced?
opts: A trial of a four-day week for office staff
A new law on working hours
qs.why: The trial is for office staff, without cutting salaries.

qs.q: How long will the trial last?
qs.why: The pilot will run for six months.

qs.q: What worry do critics have?
opts: Staff may be exhausted by the same work in fewer days
qs.why: They fear employees will cram the same workload into fewer days and burn out.

script:
Sam: Listen, Jo, there's something I need to get off my chest. The dishes have been piling up in the sink for days.
Jo: Oh, I'm sorry. I've been swamped with deadlines at work.
Sam: I get that, but it's not the first time. I don't want this to turn into a row.
Jo: No, you're right. I should have said something sooner. Why don't we draw up a cleaning rota?
Sam: That would make things much easier. As long as we both stick to it, I think we'll avoid this in future.
Jo: Agreed. I'll start tonight and do the washing-up.

qs.q: How does the conversation end?
opts: They decide to find a new flat
They agree on a plan to share chores
qs.why: They agree to make a cleaning rota.

qs.q: Why hasn't Jo done the dishes?
opts: Jo has been very busy at work
qs.why: Jo says deadlines at work have kept Jo swamped.

qs.q: What does 'get something off my chest' mean?
opts: say what has been bothering me
qs.why: Sam wants to talk about something that has been bothering Sam.

script: Good morning, everyone. Let me give you a quick rundown of where we stand at the end of the third quarter. Revenue came in at twelve percent above forecast, largely thanks to the new subscription model. However, we shouldn't get carried away: customer churn has ticked up slightly, and our support costs have risen as a result. Going forward, we'll be prioritising retention over acquisition. That means investing in onboarding, and, if necessary, putting the planned expansion into Asia on the back burner until next year. I'll send out the detailed figures after this call.

qs.q: What is the speaker doing?
qs.why: The speaker reviews the quarter and says the company will prioritise retention.

qs.q: What helped revenue exceed the forecast?
qs.why: Revenue was up largely thanks to the new subscription model.

qs.q: What does 'put on the back burner' mean?
qs.why: The expansion would wait until next year.

script: Welcome back to Tech Weekly. This week, European lawmakers have agreed on stricter proposed rules for companies that build artificial intelligence systems. Under the new framework, firms will have to disclose what data their models were trained on, and high-risk applications, such as those used in hiring, will face mandatory audits. Industry groups have pushed back, claiming the requirements could stifle innovation, particularly among start-ups that lack legal teams. Supporters counter that without clear safeguards, public trust will erode. Whether the rules strike the right balance remains to be seen, as enforcement would not begin until two years after approval.

qs.q: What is the main topic of the podcast?
opts: New European rules for AI companies
A ban on using AI in hiring
qs.why: Lawmakers agreed on stricter rules for AI companies.

qs.q: Why do industry groups object to the rules?
opts: They want audits only for start-ups
They fear the rules could hold back innovation, especially in start-ups
qs.why: They say the requirements could stifle innovation, particularly for start-ups.

qs.q: What does 'remains to be seen' suggest?
qs.why: The effect of the rules is not yet known, since enforcement would start only years from now.

script: Hello, Mr. Alvarez, it's Karen from Horizon Travel. I'm afraid I have some bad news. Your connecting flight in Chicago has been pushed back by three hours due to a storm, which means you'll miss your onward flight to Denver. I've already rebooked you on the last flight tonight, departing at ten-forty, and I've also arranged a hotel voucher in case that one gets cancelled as well. Should you prefer to fly out tomorrow morning, just let me know by seven this evening, and I'll switch it. Don't hesitate to call me back, since I'll be in the office until eight.

qs.q: Why is Karen calling?
opts: To explain a flight disruption and the new arrangements
qs.why: A storm delays his connection, and she explains what she has done.

qs.q: What has Karen already done?
opts: Rebooked him on a later flight
Booked him on a morning flight
qs.why: She rebooked him on the last flight tonight.

qs.q: Why did Karen arrange a hotel voucher?
opts: The later flight might also be cancelled
qs.why: The voucher is in case the later flight gets cancelled too.

script:
Member: Hi, I'd like to cancel my membership, please.
Advisor: Oh, I'm sorry to hear that. May I ask why?
Member: Mainly because I've been travelling so much for work that I hardly ever come in.
Advisor: I see. Well, rather than cancelling outright, we could freeze your membership for up to six months at a reduced fee.
Member: That's tempting, but I'd rather make a clean break. Besides, I've signed up for a cheaper gym near the office.
Advisor: Understood. Bear in mind that you'll need to give thirty days' notice, so your last payment will be next month.
Member: Fair enough. Where do I sign?

qs.q: What does the member want to do?
qs.why: The member asks to cancel at the start and insists on it later.

qs.q: Why does the member hardly ever use the gym?
opts: Work trips keep the member away
qs.why: The member travels a lot for work.

qs.q: What does 'make a clean break' mean here?
qs.why: The member refuses the freeze option and prefers to end the membership entirely.
